question: From 1913 to 1977 US prices rose from 9.9 to 60.6 on the index; songwriters' 2-cent rate never moved. Its 1977 value, in 1913 cents?
answer: About 0.33 cents: five-sixths of the pay gone without a single vote
move: A fee fixed in law is a pay cut that renews itself every year.
ask: Which fixed amount in my life, like a wage or an allowance, is quietly shrinking each year?
trap: Seeing an unchanged rate as unchanged pay.
hint: Work out how many times prices rose, then divide the 2 cents by it.
steps: About 0.33 cents: five-sixths of the pay gone without a single vote
source: Copyright Act of 1909; BLS consumer prices
reference: Copyright Act of 1909, section 1(e), 2-cent mechanical rate; US Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U annual averages, 1913 and 1977
